http://www.russiaherald.com/news/2792632.text: Ukraine has morphed into Zelensky's 'concentration camp' - Moscow RT.com 25 Aug 2026, 07:14 GMT+10 Kiev has descended into repression at home and "outright terror" against Russian civilians, Moscow's UN envoy has said Ukraine has been transformed into a "Zelensky concentration camp" with Western assistance, Russia's envoy to the UN, Vassily Nebenzia, has said, accusing Kiev of suppressing dissent at home and increasingly resorting to attacks on civilians in Russia. Nebenzia made the remarks at a UN Security Council meeting on Monday marking the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's declaration of independence. The session was requested by the Council's five European members - Denmark, France, Greece, Latvia and the UK - who reiterated their full political and military support for Kiev. The Russian diplomat questioned whether Ukraine had anything to celebrate, arguing that successive governments had run the country "into the ground" and that Vladimir Zelensky had accelerated the process. "With the most active involvement of the countries of the collective West, which claim to be 'civilized' and 'democratic,' Ukraine has morphed into a 'Zelensky concentration camp,' where any dissent or opposition is completely prohibited and those who find the courage to voice an alternative point of view are thrown behind bars without trial or due process, or physically eliminated," he said. Nebenzia described the persecution of the canonical Ukrainian Orthodox Church, the glorification of Nazi collaborators, and the suppression of shared history and the Russian language - including a comical ban on a popular Russian cartoon - as a "vivid illustration of the sheer wretchedness of Kiev's rulers." Amid a growing crackdown on dissent and a deteriorating battlefield situation , Kiev has now slipped into "outright terror against Russia's civilian population," Nebenzia argued. "Terror has become the last resort for Kiev in its attempt to reverse the situation that is not currently in its favor," the diplomat said. "At the same time, Zelensky continues to beg his Western patrons for new shipments of weapons and ammunition, which are then used to hit Russian cities, residential areas and civilian infrastructure." READ MORE: Three minors dead after Ukrainian attack on childcare center - official The envoy said at least 475 Russian civilians were killed or injured in Ukrainian attacks between August 10 and 16 alone, with 69 fatalities, including children. He highlighted a strike on Nizhnekamsk that killed 13 people and wounded 78, as well as attacks in Novorossiysk, the Rostov Region and multiple towns in Donbass, which Kiev claims as its territory. "It appears that Ukraine's Western patrons, not to mention Zelensky himself, still harbor the dangerous illusion that further escalation, strikes deep inside our territory and terror against civilians will somehow force us to accept an ultimatum that is being pushed under the guise of peace," he said. The Russian envoy insisted that Moscow retains the battlefield initiative and rejected calls for a temporary ceasefire that he said would merely give Kiev time to regroup and its Western sponsors time to rearm it. He warned that there would be no meaningful diplomatic process as long as Russia is confronted with ultimatums and threats while the realities on the ground are ignored. Photograph: Atef Safadi/EPA West Bank Israeli forces overwhelmed by violent settlers in ‘terrorist attack’ on Palestinian family Settler violence in West Bank makes everyday life ‘untenable’ for Palestinians, says ICRC after assault on family trying to return home in Jalud Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem Wed 30 Sep 2026 10.54 EDT First published on Wed 30 Sep 2026 10.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has said Israeli settler violence in the West Bank has made everyday life for Palestinians “untenable”, as a mob attack on Palestinians trying to return home prompted one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rivals to warn of a campaign of settler terror. More than 100 militant settlers overwhelmed Israeli security forces early on Tuesday to attack a Palestinian family as they attempted to reclaim their homes which had been seized by settlers in the West Bank village of Jalud. Three Israeli security officials were injured and houses were set on fire. The impotence of the Israeli military, the scale of the assault and the injuries inflicted on Israeli security officers by settlers prompted unusually harsh condemnation from Israeli politicians and commenters. Israel is facing unprecedented international pressure over surging violence in the occupied West Bank, where settler militants backed by cabinet ministers have accelerated a campaign of ethnic cleansing ahead of Israel’s elections next month. Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, condemned the attacks in Jalud as a “moral stain”. Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief and Netanyahu’s leading challenger in the upcoming elections, called for action to halt a “campaign of terror and violence”. Deadlier attacks by Israeli settlers, including ones targeting Palestinian children, have drawn less attention inside Israel. “Palestinian rights or safety are not the concern, even for people who are in the opposition,” said Mairav Zonszein, a senior analyst on Israel-Palestine with International Crisis Group. “The settler violence is an issue [for them] because it’s making Israel look bad, and also the idea that the military is losing control.” View image in fullscreen A Palestinian family were attacked as they attempted to reclaim their homes which had been seized by settlers in Jalud. Photograph: Atef Safadi/EPA The ICRC said attacks, settlement expansion and severe restrictions on movement were making everyday life untenable for Palestinian civilians, who Israel has a responsibility to protect under international law. . “The frequent and severe violence must be brought to an end,” said Julien Lerisson, the head of the ICRC’s delegation for Israel and Palestine. “What international humanitarian law says on the protection of private and public property, and on the population’s access to essential services, must be respected.” A graphic showing number of Palestinians killed in the West Bank by settlers or Israeli civilians A bar on imports of settlement goods came into force in the Netherlands last week, the UK has announced plans for even broader controls on trade and financing of settlements, and a similar bill will be introduced in the US legislature on Thursday. ‘The settlers brought the violence’: the ethnic cleansing of a West Bank village Read more On Tuesday, a Senate bill demanding a human rights report on Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was narrowly defeated after winning backing from all but one Democrat. “Tonight a disaster was averted, but the barrier has been broken,” the Israeli analyst Roy Sharon wrote on social media after the vote, warning that “anarchy in the West Bank” may cost Israel military aid from the US and its international legitimacy. A cartoon in Israel’s largest-circulation newspaper, Yedioth Ahronoth, on Wednesday showed two soldiers watching an arson attack on a Palestinian home. “They’re going to ruin my trip to Amsterdam,” one says to the other. More than 60 Palestinian communities in the occupied West Bank have been wiped off the map since October 2023 and 18 others have been partly displaced, according to the Israeli rights group B’Tselem. Nearly 5,000 people have been forced from their homes, almost half of them children. View image in fullscreen Mahmod Tubasi, 60, and his wife, Aedah, 51, and their family had been forced out of their homes this summer by settler militants. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters The Tubasi family, whose homes were burned in Jalud, had been forced out this summer after a weeks-long siege by settler militants. Last week they secured a high court ruling ordering the Israeli state to evict settlers and secure their return. Late on Monday the Israeli military told the family that about 15 military police officers would escort them home immediately, Israel’s Haaretz newspaper reported. That was a small number given that Israel is celebrating the Sukkot holiday. The number of violent extremists in illegal settlements usually rises during festivals, and the force was outnumbered by a violent crowd within minutes of arriving. “To carry out an operation such as this, and during the holiday of Sukkot when the [settler] outposts are packed, is madness,” a security source said. The military had not informed national police and the Shin Bet domestic intelligence service of their plans, so they had no security backup. Settlers attacked a house when the Tubasi family arrived, forcing them to the roof, before the military decided to evacuate them in armoured military vehicles. The crowd then set the homes on fire, blocked roads and threw stones at Israeli security forces, injuring three personnel. The two houses “were damaged beyond description”, said Wael ​Tubasi. “They damaged everything – the doors, the tiles were removed, the stairs were removed. They smashed the bathrooms, doors and windows. They left nothing, everything was broken,” he told Reuters. View image in fullscreen The Tubasi family’s homes were ‘damaged beyond description’, said Wael Tubasi. ‘Everything was broken.’ Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters Earlier this year the former prime minister Ehud Olmert called for the international criminal court to intervene to stop settler violence because the state had failed. Netanyahu condemned the “violent riots” and called for prosecution of the attackers, but defended the illegal settler movement. “The handful of rioters are not representative of the law-abiding settler public in Judea and Samaria,” the prime minister said, using an Israeli term for the occupied West Bank. A landmark 2024 ruling from the UN’s international court of justice found that the occupation violated international law, a position the British government has endorsed. An Israeli military spokesperson said two suspects had been detained, and called for action to tackle settler militants who targeted Israeli security forces. “The violence directed at soldiers while they were carrying out their duties crosses a clear red line and is unacceptable,” the spokesperson said. “There is no place for such incidents in the state of Israel, and they must not be allowed to become the norm. Such phenomena must be addressed at their root.” On Wednesday, some in Israel questioned whether the army and the state had the capacity to do that. “We have to look reality squarely in the eye: this was a terrorist attack and a failure by the Israeli defence establishment in its entirety,” Avi Ashkenazi wrote in the Maariv newspaper. “It is clear at this point that the real sovereign in Judea and Samaria are the extreme rightwing terrorist activists.” Explore more on these topics West Bank Palestine Israel International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) Middle East and north Africa news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story UN adds 61 firms to settlements blacklist over alleged human rights violations against Palestinians Senior UK rabbis come out in support of sanctions on Israeli settlements Miliband rejects chief rabbi’s claim that West Bank sanctions put UK Jews at risk Will UK sanctions have any impact on Israel’s ‘settler terrorists’ in West Bank?
